newsitem.title: USA: U.S. foreign crude business quiet, Brent deal done.
newsitem.headline: U.S. foreign crude business quiet, Brent deal done.

text.p: Foreign crude business into the U.S.was quiet for most of Monday, though some Brent paper trades appeared later in the afternoon.
Traders said the feature of the session was a physical Brent deal, done at slightly weaker levels than last deals seen Friday.
Brokers confirmed a September 7-9 Brent cargo was sold at September paper minus 25 cents, putting the dated Brent value at $20.55-$20.65.
IPE Brent was closed Monday for holiday. Business will resume Tuesday, and likely repeat the down moves on the NYMEX.
Late in the U.S. aftermarket window, traders recorded a modest pick-up in the level of activity. October paper Brent partial cargoes were bought at $19.98, $19.99 and $20.00.
Brent spreads were sold at 38 cents in Oct/Nov, and at 42 cents for Sep/Oct.
Oct NYMEX futures shed 34 cents at $21.62 a barrel. IPE Oct Brent will start Tuesday at $20.41, Friday's settlement.
Crude brokers said Latin American talk was quiet, as were other North Sea grades.
